text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday concern about the environment was now a feature of mainstream Australia.
"Concern about the environment is no longer a cafe society pre-occupation," Howard told the 3M Australian Conservation Foundation Forsite Conference.
The environment had not received enough attention in the past, but warned that everyone had a part to play in ensuring that it was given sufficient attention, he said.
"If we are to have a credible approach to environmental care and environmental concern in the years ahead, they must receive far greater attention," he said.
"It requires a government that is prepared to treat environmental concerns at the top of the political agenda ... and it also needs the preoccupation and concern of the business community," he said.
The government hopes to outlay A$1.0 billion for the establishment of an natural heritage trust.
The trust will be funded from the planned A$8.0 billion sale of a third of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp, which is currently before the upper house of parliament, the Senate.
